correctness.rationale: For φ(0)=0, write A(z)=φ(z)/z; Schwarz–Pick gives lower control on |1-A|/(1-|z|²) when b=A(0)≠1, hence any Berezin values approaching 1 have preimages approaching zero. Expansion Bφ(z)=1+(b-1)|z|²+O(|z|³) forces all range points onto the same affine real line under convexity. For each r<1 the auxiliary holomorphic F_r(ζ)=(1-r²)/(1-r²A(ζ)) takes its radius-r boundary values on that line; the harmonic maximum principle and open mapping force F_r and A constant. Real-line containment and the limit Bφ→0 imply b real; direct monotone parametrization gives (0,1] for -1≤b<1, singleton {1} for b=1. The estimates also handle |b|=1 and the identity case. Finite diagnostics are not the universal proof.
